name: Bali
dek: Precipitation only, from the Japan Meteorological Agency's 1991–2020 normal for Denpasar.
paragraphs: The Indonesian 1991–2020 submission in the NOAA NCEI collection has two Bali files, Stasiun Meteorologi I Gusti Ngurah Rai (97230) and Stasiun Geofisika Denpasar (97232), and neither prints monthly values. The rain column is the Japan Meteorological Agency's 1991–2020 normal for station 97230, listed as Denpasar (8.75°S, 115.17°E, 1 m), computed from the CLIMAT reports BMKG sends through the WMO. January is the wettest month, at 350.7 mm, and July the driest, at 27.6 mm. Bali keeps a different time zone from Jakarta. The same JMA page gives the 1991–2020 normal monthly mean temperature in °C as Jan 27.9, Feb 28.0, Mar 28.0, Apr 28.1, May 27.8, Jun 27.2, Jul 26.5, Aug 26.3, Sep 26.8, Oct 27.6, Nov 28.2, Dec 28.0; the table has no column for a mean, so those figures are printed here.
The plug, currency, and entry lines are national and repeat the Indonesia sheet. No official tipping source was found on this pass, so that line is missing.

climate.caption: Station: Denpasar, WMO 97230. Precipitation only.
climate.note: Normals from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) ClimatView tool, which computes 1991–2020 normals from the CLIMAT reports national services send through the WMO. ClimatView gives a normal for monthly mean temperature and precipitation only; it has no normal daily maximum or minimum, so the high and low cells are blank. BMKG publishes the underlying observations, but a BMKG 1991–2020 monthly table for Bali was not found on this pass, and the BMKG files in the NOAA NCEI collection print no Bali values.
climate.sourceTitle: Japan Meteorological Agency, ClimatView monthly statistics, station 97230

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type C and F, 220 V and 110 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows Indonesia at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read. The line lists two voltages and does not say where each is used, so this sheet does not either.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: Law 22 of 2009 on Road Traffic and Transport, Article 108(1), says road users must use the left lane of the road; the right lane is for overtaking or when directed by police.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Indonesia, last reviewed August 25, 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Rupiah and the code IDR for Indonesia.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab and zone1970.tab put Bali on the Asia/Makassar row, commented east and south Borneo, Sulawesi/Celebes, Bali, Nusa Tengarra, and west Timor. Jakarta is on Asia/Jakarta, a different zone.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: The official e-Visa site of the immigration directorate. We do not restate a visa rule.
